Having found what I came for, I was too hasty to leave and fell afoul of this trap. I'm not strong enough to prise the teeth apart, and every moment I grow weaker as the pool of blood around me expands. I am soon to die in this dark, awful place, but perhaps I can help you.

After years of exploration and toil I finally located Harland's Spyglass. It's the final location on my list, of course. Why is everything always in the last place one looks?

EN:
My colleagues and I have found yet another point to disagree on. However many times I am proved right, they must try me again and again. They've invited a young apprentice to join our wizardly conclave. He smells of the gutter to me, but Mezzentious vouchsafed him so I kept my counsel to myself--much to my regret!

It was a matter of days before we discovered him stealing, and when we confronted the little rat, he had the stones to actually fight us! He held his own for several minutes, a confusing state of affairs, until I caught him with a bolt of dark magic. 

He should have been reduced to ashes, but the blackguard shrugged it off and kept going. Shortly thereafter, he escaped.|NEXTPAGE|As for a slender youth fighting us to a draw, I think I already knew the answer by then. In addition to its other properties, the cloak is disguised as a dull, weathered garment, something you might see a grain merchant wearing. When I arrived home my fears were confirmed: my Chameleon Cloak had been stolen!

But we three are not quite as doddering as we appear. Unbeknownst to our thief, Colophon cast a simple cantrip of tracking before he slipped away, so we know exactly where to find him. I sketched out the location below so that later I may gaze upon it whilst savoring the thief's destruction!

EN:
Dearest Brother,

I trust you recall me writing about Master Porvidius's "special orders," which have made him the richest cobbler within 50 leagues--well, the mystery is solved!

One fiercely cold night, I left the shop early, claiming a sour stomach, then circled back an hour later. All was dark and at first I thought the shop was empty, but the master was down in the cellar. That space is only used for storage, or so I thought.|NEXTPAGE|The bastard has an imp imprisoned in a secret room, trapped in a magic circle! He forces the creature to enchant his shoes and boots--not all of them of course, only one or two pairs of his finest every year. If the magistrates discovered Master Porvidius working this wicked magic he would be soundly flogged, and likely face a stiff fine. The latter would pain him more, I'm certain.|NEXTPAGE|Now I am the owner of a pair of enchanted boots, and instead of earning coppers as a lowly apprentice I plan to make my way in the world as a blackmailer! I've already packed my things and slipped away with the prize. But should the theft be reported before I have time to get my affairs in order, I hid the boots away. If anything happens to me, they're in a cave where I used to stop and sit for a quiet smoke when I needed to get away from the family. But I know how your memory can be, so I've attached a map just in case.

Yours in prosperity,
Stephen
